title: Capivasertib + fulvestrant
context_label: Gene-altered, ER-positive / HER2-negative advanced breast cancer
schedule_label: Four days on / three off, with fulvestrant injections
schedule_summary: Capivasertib is taken twice daily for four days, then stopped for three days, each week. Fulvestrant injections are given on Days 1 and 15 of the first 28-day cycle, then Day 1 of later cycles. Treatment continues while helpful and tolerated.
purpose: This combination aims to control advanced breast cancer. Capivasertib blocks a growth signal inside cancer cells and fulvestrant reduces signalling through the oestrogen receptor. Tumour testing helps identify people whose cancer has a relevant pathway alteration.
indication_text: For adults whose ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer has a PIK3CA, AKT1 or PTEN change and has grown during or after hormone treatment. The team also checks general health and earlier treatment.
administration_text: The usual starting capivasertib dose is 400 mg twice daily, about 12 hours apart, on the prescribed dosing days. Swallow tablets whole, with or without food; avoid grapefruit. Your prescription may use a lower dose. Each usual 500 mg fulvestrant dose is two slow injections into muscle, one in each buttock; no IV port or pump is required.
monitoring_summary: Check blood count, kidney and liver function before treatment and each cycle. Check fasting glucose and HbA1c before starting. Fasting glucose is checked at weeks 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8, then monthly; ideally before the tablet dose on day 3 or 4 of a dosing week. HbA1c is checked every three months, with an extra week-4 check for diabetes, prediabetes or high baseline glucose. Diabetes, new high glucose or metformin initiation needs extra checks under a written plan.
review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

agents.name: Capivasertib
agents.alias: Tablets twice daily for four days, followed by three days without these tablets, every week
agents.explanation: Blocks AKT1, AKT2 and AKT3, proteins that help carry growth and survival signals inside cells. PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alterations can activate this pathway. AKT also helps the body respond to insulin. Blocking it can raise blood sugar, which is why glucose checks start early.
risks: Raised blood sugar or diabetes; rarely a dangerous ketone/acidity problem called diabetic ketoacidosis
Rash, itch or severe skin reactions
Nausea, vomiting, sore mouth, reduced appetite and tiredness
Changes in blood counts or kidney/liver tests, assessed by the team
agents.mechanism: Blocks an internal growth signal called AKT
visual: The tumour has a relevant pathway alteration
Growth and survival signals are reduced
agents.watch: Keep the glucose plan and report diarrhoea, rash or high-glucose symptoms early.

agents.name: Fulvestrant
agents.alias: Two injections into the buttock muscles at each treatment visit
agents.explanation: Attaches to oestrogen receptors and reduces their number, making it harder for oestrogen to stimulate hormone-sensitive breast cancer.
risks: Pain, bruising or bleeding at the injection sites; rarely nerve injury symptoms
Hot flushes and joint or muscle discomfort
Nausea, tiredness and changes in liver tests
Allergic reactions; discuss pregnancy prevention and fertility
visual: Less oestrogen-driven signalling reaches the cell
agents.watch: Report unusual injection-site bleeding, severe pain, numbness or pain travelling down the leg.

sources.title: Turner NC et al. Capivasertib in Hormone Receptor-Positive Advanced Breast Cancer. NEJM 2023;388:2058–2070.

anatomy: New thirst, passing more urine or marked tiredness: contact the team promptly.
Start the agreed diarrhoea plan; seek help if severe, persistent or you cannot drink.
Report new rash or mouth soreness. Blistering or peeling needs urgent help.
Report bruising, unusual bleeding, radiating leg pain, numbness or weakness.
Support is available for flushes and joint or muscle symptoms.
Report jaw pain, loose teeth or a wound that does not heal, particularly with bone-modifying treatment.
anatomy_note: Selected effects are linked to the relevant medicine. Symptoms can occur on dosing days or tablet-free days; the map is not a complete list.

monitoring_schedule.note: Planned review points are not equal time intervals or booked tests. Fasting glucose is preferably checked before the dose on day 3 or 4 of a dosing week. The team agrees additional home monitoring.

urgent_extra: Seek urgent assessment for unusual thirst or urination, severe diarrhoea, inability to drink, or a new rash. Vomiting with abdominal pain, breathing difficulty, fruity breath, confusion or marked sleepiness can signal ketoacidosis: seek emergency help without waiting for a high glucose reading. Blistering or peeling skin also needs urgent help.

sections.title: Injection visits and extra tests
sections.text: Two fulvestrant injection visits in the first cycle, then one every 28 days. Glucose and other monitoring can create extra checks between injection visits.

sections.title: Tablets and supply
sections.text: Capivasertib tablet strengths are 160 mg and 200 mg. The team confirms the correct number and strength for the prescribed dose; retain the recurring four-day/three-day calendar.

sections.title: Access and practical planning
sections.text: No IV port, infusion or take-home pump is required by this two-medicine regimen. Additional treatments may have separate arrangements.

sections.title: Missed doses and pauses
sections.text: If a capivasertib dose is late, it may be taken within 4 hours of its usual time, leaving at least 8 hours before the next dose. If more than 4 hours late, skip it and take the next dose at the usual time. Do not double a dose. If you vomit after a dose, do not take an extra dose; take the next scheduled dose at its usual time. Contact the team if vomiting continues or prevents fluids or medicines.

sections.title: Your support contacts
sections.text: Agree daytime and out-of-hours contacts, access to glucose testing, and what to do if a test, prescription or injection appointment is missing.

evidence.title: Why this combination may be chosen
evidence.intro: The medicines work on different signals involved in hormone-sensitive cancer. Your team chooses the combination using the cancer tests, earlier treatment and your health, and checks both benefit and side effects as treatment continues.
evidence.population: Gene-altered, ER-positive / HER2-negative advanced breast cancer
evidence.interpretation: The combination can delay worsening of the cancer in the selected group. A longer overall survival has not been established in the final trial analysis.
evidence.limitations: Discuss your own expected benefit, alternatives and treatment burden with the team. Trial averages cannot predict an individual outcome.

teachback: Which days have capivasertib, which three days are tablet-free, when are the injections and glucose checks, and which symptoms need urgent help?
consent_support: Discuss glucose/diabetes and ketoacidosis, diarrhoea/dehydration, skin reactions and injection risks. Agree the tablet pattern, glucose plan and contact route. Pregnancy and breastfeeding are excluded. Contraception advice must cover the longer fulvestrant period: two years after its last dose for women; capivasertib male advice extends sixteen weeks after stopping. Discuss fertility and the individual plan.

support.title: Glucose plan
support.text: Agree when to check glucose and when to call. Use your written diabetes-medicine plan on tablet-taking and tablet-free days; do not change existing diabetes medicines yourself.

support.title: Diarrhoea and fluids
support.text: Have the prescribed diarrhoea medicine available. Follow the agreed early-treatment instructions and contact the team for persistent symptoms, dizziness or reduced urine.

support.title: Skin and injections
support.text: Report rash early and use skin treatments as advised. Tell the injector about anticoagulants, bruising and any previous leg nerve symptoms.

chapters.title: The treatment being discussed
chapters.intro: This combination aims to control advanced breast cancer. Capivasertib blocks a growth signal inside cancer cells and fulvestrant reduces signalling through the oestrogen receptor. Tumour testing helps identify people whose cancer has a relevant pathway alteration.

items.title: Who this regimen covers
items.text: For adults whose ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer has a PIK3CA, AKT1 or PTEN change and has grown during or after hormone treatment. The team also checks general health and earlier treatment.

items.title: Taking the tablets
items.text: Take capivasertib with or without food and swallow the tablets whole with water. Do not chew, crush, split or dissolve them. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.

items.title: Injection visits
items.text: 500 mg intramuscularly as two 5 mL injections, one in each buttock, slowly over 1–2 minutes per injection. Cycle 1: days 1 and 15. Cycle 2 onward: day 1 of each 28-day cycle.

items.title: Ovarian suppression and pregnancy
items.text: If you are pre- or perimenopausal, a separately prescribed medicine must suppress ovarian hormone production with this combination. The team may also consider this for men. Age alone does not confirm suppression. Discuss fertility, pregnancy prevention and breastfeeding. Follow the longer fulvestrant contraception advice: two years after its last dose for women; capivasertib advice for men extends sixteen weeks after stopping. Your team confirms the individual plan.

chapters.title: Glucose and other checks
chapters.intro: Some checks happen between injection visits. Agree who books them and who reviews the results.

items.title: Starting and continuing checks
items.text: Check blood count, kidney and liver function before treatment and each cycle. Check fasting glucose and HbA1c before starting. Fasting glucose is checked at weeks 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8, then monthly; ideally before the tablet dose on day 3 or 4 of a dosing week. HbA1c is checked every three months, with an extra week-4 check for diabetes, prediabetes or high baseline glucose. Diabetes, new high glucose or metformin initiation needs extra checks under a written plan.

items.title: If you already have diabetes
items.text: Check fasting glucose daily for the first two weeks, then as often as the team advises. An extra HbA1c is recommended at week 4 when diabetes, prediabetes or high baseline glucose is present.

items.title: If glucose rises
items.text: The team may arrange at least twice-weekly checks, including tablet-taking and tablet-free days, and ketone tests or specialist review. Follow the written plan; symptoms can need urgent assessment even without a very high reading.

items.title: If metformin is started
items.text: The team checks kidney function weekly for up to three weeks after metformin starts with capivasertib, then on Day 1 of each cycle. Existing diabetes treatment needs individual reconciliation.

chapters.title: Support between treatment visits
chapters.intro: Early reporting helps the team treat symptoms and review doses safely.

items.title: Diarrhoea plan
items.text: Have the agreed anti-diarrhoea plan available before starting. NCCP gives loperamide 4 mg at first onset, then 2 mg after each loose stool, up to 16 mg in a day. Increase oral fluids and contact the team promptly for severe or persistent diarrhoea, inability to drink, dizziness, reduced urine or palpitations. Secondary prevention can be considered for recurrent diarrhoea.

items.title: Skin plan
items.text: Report a new rash promptly. Use moisturisers and any antihistamine or cream prescribed for your symptoms. Do not start steroids or change doses without review.

items.title: Medicine review
items.text: Tell the team about every prescription, non-prescription or herbal product. New medicines can change capivasertib exposure and require a reviewed dose.

items.title: Cancer response
items.text: Your team agrees which scans or other tests you need and when, and reviews symptoms, treatment benefit and your priorities.

questions.q: What if I miss or vomit a capivasertib dose?
questions.a: If a capivasertib dose is late, it may be taken within 4 hours of its usual time, leaving at least 8 hours before the next dose. If more than 4 hours late, skip it and take the next dose at the usual time. Do not double a dose. If you vomit after a dose, do not take an extra dose; take the next scheduled dose at its usual time. Contact the team if vomiting continues or prevents fluids or medicines.

questions.q: Do the three tablet-free days also change my diabetes medicines?
questions.a: Follow the individual written plan from the oncology and diabetes teams. Glucose can fall on tablet-free days. Do not automatically stop or continue a changed diabetes dose without the agreed instructions.
Pre- or perimenopausal women need a separately prescribed LHRH medicine with this combination. The team may also consider this for men. Age alone does not confirm suppression.

questions.q: What if the tablets are paused?
questions.a: Contact the team for a revised plan. Do not restart or increase capivasertib yourself, and do not assume a tablet pause cancels or resets the fulvestrant injection schedule.

questions.q: How long is treatment and how will benefit be assessed?
questions.a: There is no fixed number of cycles. The team reviews cancer symptoms, scans, tolerability and priorities, and continues or changes treatment accordingly.

phase_cycles.label: Cycle 1 · extra fulvestrant loading visit
phase_cycles.schedule_summary: Capivasertib is taken twice daily for four days, then stopped for three days, each week. Fulvestrant injections are given on Days 1 and 15 of the first 28-day cycle, then Day 1 of later cycles. Treatment continues while helpful and tolerated.

timeline.label: Glucose symptoms / checks
timeline.text: Follow the written plan throughout the week

phase_cycles.label: Cycle 2 onward · one fulvestrant visit per cycle
phase_cycles.schedule_summary: The same four-days-on/three-days-off capivasertib pattern continues. Fulvestrant is given on Day 1 of each 28-day cycle, without the extra Day 15 loading visit.

timeline.label: Glucose symptoms / checks
timeline.text: Follow the written plan throughout the week

timeline_note: Tablet days and injection days follow the prescribed regimen. Side effects can occur at any time and are not predicted by the width of a band.
safety_note: Tablet-free days still require symptom reporting and the agreed glucose checks. The treatment calendar does not authorise a dose or restart.

chronology_notes.title: Weekly tablet breaks
chronology_notes.text: Days 5–7, 12–14, 19–21 and 26–28 have no planned capivasertib. Do not replace these with seven continuous treatment days.

chronology_notes.title: Different medicine schedules
chronology_notes.text: The extra Day 15 fulvestrant dose belongs to cycle 1. Changes to one medicine require review of the other, not an automatic cancellation.
